page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.large is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, ranking in the top 25% across Geekbench single-core (1939.0) and stress-ng single-core tests (3059.78). However, parallel execution metrics reflect the single-core physical constraint: Geekbench multi-core (2433.0) and PassMark CPU (3799.5) place in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is mixed, offering 27.53 GB/s for large uncached block writes, but dropping to bottom percentiles for small cached block reads (150.55 GB/s). Workload benchmarks show 2.83 million operations per second for Redis SET commands, alongside lower throughput for database operations and static web serving (2.79 GB/s).

Given its high per-core computational throughput and modern vector instructions, the ecs.c8a.large offers favorable entry-level compute efficiency for workloads that rely heavily on single-thread performance rather than parallel throughput or memory capacity. Primary operational fits include lightweight microservices, task runners, CI/CD worker nodes, and basic web application serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.large is a compute-optimized instance provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, it follows a 1:2 compute-focused resource ratio. It includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network volumes, and delivers 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, though aggregate multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles due to the two-thread ceiling. The ecs.c8a.large serves as an efficient compute configuration for low-concurrency backend services, CI/CD processing tasks, and single-threaded application modules.
